sentences.text: Unknown vs Sandeep Subha" on 22 May, 2023

Author: Sharad Kumar Sharma
Bench: Sharad Kumar Sharma
 Office Notes,
 reports, orders
Sl. or proceedings or
 Date Court'S Or Judges'S Order
S No directions and  Registrar's order  with Signatures  C482 No.268 of 2023  Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Pramod Kumar, learned counsel holding brief of Mr. Raj Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicants.
Mr. A.K. Sah, learned Deputy Advocate General along with Mr. Mamta Joshi, learned Brief Holder for the State.
Mr. Shailendra Nauriyal, learned counsel for the private respondents.

The applicant is facing a proceedings of Criminal Case No.4751 of 2021, State Vs. Sandeep Subha",
which has been instituted by respondent no.3, the brother of the deceased respondent no.2, who was the wife of the applicant.
Owing to certain matrimonial discord, the respondent no.2/ (deceased) complainant, has registered an FIR, being FIR No.33 of 2021, dated 18.01.2021 for the involvement of the applicant in commission of offences under Section 498-A, 323, 504 and 494 of the IPC, on which the summoning order has been issued after the culmination of the investigation by the court of learned 1st Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, District Dehradun resulting into registration of Criminal Case No.4751 of 2021, "State Vs. Sandeep Subba".

entities.text: 1st Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, District Dehradun
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Apart from the aforesaid proceedings, there also happens to be a complaint proceeding also which has been drawn by the deceased respondent no.2, as against the present applicant by registering a case before the court of learned 1st Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dehradun "Anita Subba Vs.
Sandeep Kumar Subba" for the offences under Section 323, 494, 495, 504 and 506 of the IPC.

entities.text:
Anita Subba Vs.
Sandeep Kumar Subba
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This Court was initially of the view that since the dispute happens to be of a matrimonial in nature,
the parties could be persuaded to enter into a settlement.

But, owing to the complexity of relationship, which the present applicant has with the brother of the deceased complainant and,
apart from the fact that, since there are various other proceedings which already going on against Unknown vs Sandeep Subha" on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102010344/
1

the present applicant and since there has been expressed denial by respondent no.3, that he is not in a position to make any effort for settlement, the settlement proceedings, as such, would hereby stand dropped.

But, so far as the institution of the proceedings of Criminal Case No.4751 of 2021 is concerned,
looking to the contents of the FIR, which is almost similar to the complaint proceedings drawn by the deceased complainant/ respondent no.2, all the set of allegations they are required to be established by appreciation of evidence by the learned trial Court, after conducting the trial into the set of allegations levelled against the present applicant.

I do not see any reason as to why the court should venture into the proceedings under Sections 498A, 323, 504 and 494 of the IPC, particularly, when the offences which are complained of though being a matrimonial dispute, they carry an element of seriousness with regards to the allegations levelled against the present applicant.

For the aforesaid reasons, this Court is not inclined to exercise its inherent power under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, the C482 Application is dismissed.

The consequential actions to follow automatically,
in accordance with law.

(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.) 22.05.2023 Sukhbant Unknown vs Sandeep Subha" on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102010344/
